value.rationale: The probability that an entire majoritarian assignment top cycle fails to contain all n! allocations is a natural measure of decisive content. The distributional theorem gives a sharp leading constant and separates the n^2-scale fixed-q logarithmic decay from the n-scale uniform decay. These are not reported by the deterministic structure theorem; the second-choice rare configurations contribute nontrivially to the coefficient. The calculation gives a precise probabilistic benchmark for a natural correlated preference model.
